Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim - Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator (QEMU functional + vsim cycle-accurate, two-phase handoff QEMU1 -> vsim).
CANONICAL docs that are the source of truth and MUST be kept (do not recommend deleting these): CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md (always-current user guide), docs/FRS.md, docs/MRD.md, ROADMAP.md (master FR tracker, "single source of truth"), driver/ROADMAP.md (C++ andes-sim driver tracker), docs/engine_interface.md, docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb (the L-id capability-gap envelope).
The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `docs/v_csr_plan.md`

Steps:
1. Read `docs/v_csr_plan.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

1	# Full V-CSR support across the hybrid handoff
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Today the QEMU1 -> vsim round trip passes V *register* data
6	(v0..v31) reliably via the `kVScratchGpa` shared-mmap stop-gap, but V
7	*CSRs* are partial:
8	
9	| Component                                    | Out (drain)                          | In (restore)                |
10	|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
11	| QEMU1 plugin (`hybrid_handoff.c`)            | vstart vtype vl vlenb + vreg         | n/a                         |
12	| vsim StateDrain (`state_drain.hpp`)          | x1..x31 + DPC; V CSRs lost           | n/a                         |
13	| vsim ResumeDriver (`resume_driver.hpp`)      | n/a                                  | mtvec only                  |
14	
15	Concrete consequences:
16	
17	1. `hybrid_state_v1` has no slots for **vxsat (0x009), vxrm (0x00A),
18	   vcsr (0x00F)**, so the ABI cannot represent the fixed-point flags or
19	   the bundled vcsr alias at any point in the pipeline.
20	2. `ResumeDriver::resume()` (resume_driver.hpp:52-85) restores only
21	   `mtvec`. Per its inline comment, mstatus/vtype/vl/vstart are
22	   "intentionally NOT restored" because vsim DM may silently drop
23	   abstract write of mstatus, and a direct CSR write of vtype sets
24	   `vill=1` per V spec, poisoning the next V instruction.
25	3. `rt_c_v_regs.c:68-72` and `:146-148` work around (2) by re-issuing
26	   `csrs mstatus, t1` and `vsetvli` inside the fixture itself. Every
27	   future V fixture would need to repeat that prologue.
28	4. `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` (state_drain.hpp:53-61) falls
29	   back on the QEMU1 snapshot for every field except GPRs and PC. If
30	   vsim mutates vstart / vxsat / vxrm / vtype / vl, those mutations
31	   never reach the drained state file.
32	5. The old QEMU2 handback (which only re-sent `vstart` + the v0..v31
33	   byte blobs and dropped vtype / vl / vxsat / vxrm / vcsr) has been
34	   removed; the pipeline is now 2-phase. vsim's drain produces the
35	   final state file, so every V CSR has to be captured there (see 4) -
36	   there is no later leg to fix it up.
37	
38	Goal: every V CSR survives the round trip transparently. Fixtures stop
39	needing inline `csrs mstatus, ...` or other compensating prologues.
40	
41	## Tiering
42	
43	V CSRs split by writability:
44	
45	- **Tier A - directly writable**: `vstart` (0x008), `vxsat` (0x009),
46	  `vxrm` (0x00A), `vcsr` (0x00F), and `mstatus.VS`. Spec-compliant to
47	  CSR-write directly. DM Abstract path is preferred; Program Buffer is
48	  the fallback when the DM rejects (`cmderr` set).
49	- **Tier B - vsetvli-only**: `vtype` (0xC21), `vl` (0xC20). V spec says
50	  direct CSR write of `vtype` sets `vill=1`; the only correct restore is
51	  `vsetvl x0, rs1, rs2`. Always Program Buffer.
52	- **Tier C - read-only**: `vlenb` (0xC22). Constant from CPU
53	  configuration (`NDS_VLEN`); verify on receive only.
54	
55	Restore order on the vsim side (each step issued via the resume driver):
56	
57	1. mstatus.VS = Initial (Tier A).
58	2. `vsetvl` to re-establish vtype + vl (Tier B).
59	3. vstart (Tier A) - written *after* vsetvl because vsetvl resets vstart
60	   to 0; non-zero values must be restored last to survive.
61	4. vxsat, vxrm, vcsr (Tier A).
62	5. Then the non-V GPR/CSR/PC restore as today.
63	
64	## Critical files
65	
66	| File                                                    | Change                                                                                                |
67	|---------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
68	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`                            | Add `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr` (consume 24 bytes from `reserved[256]`). Stay on v1.                       |
69	| `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`                      | New offset/size static_asserts for the three new fields.                                              |
70	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`                          | Resolve + drain vxsat / vxrm / vcsr alongside the existing vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb block.               |
71	| `verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` *(new)*     | Helper: stage GPR via Data0/1 -> AccessRegister, write progbufN, AccessRegister postexec=1, clear cmderr. |
72	| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`              | Tier A path with Abstract-first + PB fallback. Tier B `vsetvl` via PB. New helpers `write_csr_via_pb`, `vsetvl_via_pb`. |
73	| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`                | Read V CSRs via Abstract. Stop relying on QEMU1 passthrough for them.                                 |
74	| `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.c`                 | (Final step) drop `csrs mstatus, t1` prologues once restore is reliable.                              |
75	| `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_csrs.c` *(new)*         | Fixture seeding non-default vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm in QEMU1, mutating in vsim, verifying in the drained state file.|
76	| `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`                  | Register `rt_c_v_csrs:0` as Tier-2 fixture (csr + pc variants).                                       |
77	
78	## TDD sequence
79	
80	Each commit prefixed `structural:` or `behavioral:` per repo convention.
81	
82	1. **structural** - Extend `hybrid_state_v1` (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr from
83	   `reserved`). Update `state_abi_check.h`. Suite stays green; struct
84	   grew but nothing reads/writes the new fields yet.
85	2. **behavioral** - QEMU plugin drains vxsat/vxrm/vcsr. Verify by
86	   inspecting state file from a fixture that issues e.g. `csrwi vxrm,
87	   1; csrwi vxsat, 1` before the trigger.
88	3. **structural** - Extract `ProgramBuffer` helper + unit test on a
89	   recording stub `DmiBus`. No runtime path uses it yet.
90	4. **behavioral** - ResumeDriver Tier A: Abstract-first restore for
91	   mstatus/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr with PB fallback on cmderr. Unit-test
92	   the fallback decision against a stub bus that fails one CSR.
93	5. **behavioral** - ResumeDriver Tier B: `vsetvl` via PB. Unit-test the
94	   encoded vsetvl matches V spec for representative (sew, lmul, ta, ma)
95	   tuples.
96	6. **behavioral** - StateDrain reads V CSRs via Abstract; remove the
97	   passthrough for them in `drain_with_passthrough`.
98	7. **behavioral** - (Removed.) The QEMU2 handback leg no longer exists;
99	   vsim's drain (step 6) writes the V CSRs into the state file, which is
100	   the pipeline's final output. There is no separate P-packet ship step.
101	8. **behavioral** - New e2e fixture `rt_c_v_csrs.c`, wired as Tier-2 in
102	   `HybridConfig.cmake` (csr + pc trigger variants).
103	9. **cleanup (structural)** - Strip `csrs mstatus, t1` from
104	   `rt_c_v_regs.c`. Confirm suite stays green; restore path now carries
105	   it.
106	
107	## Verification ladder
108	
109	1. After step 1: `ctest -L hybrid-e2e` 30 PASS unchanged.
110	2. After step 4: unit test exercises Tier A Abstract->PB fallback on a
111	   synthetic DM rejecting one CSR.
112	3. After step 5: unit test asserts vsetvl encoding for SEW=8/16/32/64
113	   times LMUL=1/2/4/8 times {ta, ma}.
114	4. After step 6: existing `rt_c_v_regs` round trip still passes; vsim
115	   mutating mstatus/vtype/vl/vstart in a probe fixture is observable in
116	   the drained state file.
117	5. After step 8: `rt_c_v_csrs` PASS in both csr and pc modes; the
118	   drained state file holds exactly the values vsim left.
119	6. After step 9: `rt_c_v_regs` runs unchanged with the prologue removed.
120	   Total e2e count goes 30 -> 32 (csr + pc variant of the new fixture).
121	7. `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` total reaches 36 PASS (34 baseline + 2 new).
122	
123	## Risks
124	
125	- **vsim DM may not expose Tier A V CSRs via Abstract**. Mitigation: PB
126	  fallback is the canonical path; an orchestrator-startup probe logs
127	  which CSRs are Abstract-accessible so reachability stays observable.
128	- **Direct mstatus abstract write may be silently dropped on vsim's
129	  DM** (already noted in resume_driver.hpp:74). Mitigation: rely on
130	  PB for mstatus, treat Abstract-success as a fast path only.
131	- **GPR clobber inside PB**: PB needs scratch GPRs (t0/t1). Restore
132	  those *after* the PB sequence so the snapshot's t0/t1 survive. Order
133	  the GPR-write loop accordingly.
134	- **vlenb mismatch** (QEMU1 reports vlenb != vsim NDS_VLEN/8):
135	  unrecoverable; fail loudly at restore.
136	
137	## Out of scope
138	
139	- Phase 5 transparent V regfile transport (Program Buffer or DPI for v0..v31). Plan keeps the existing `kVScratchGpa` mechanism unchanged.
140	- Andes-custom V CSRs beyond the spec set (no fixture exercises them today).
141	- Fault state when mstatus.VS=Off at the QEMU1 trigger (current fixtures all start with V enabled).
142

commit 1af22df6c272ff29ad96a5965f158e616c97f87f
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 16 08:48:09 2026 +0800

    hybrid: trap-CSR round-trip (L24) + V-scratch reservation above program RAM (L26)
    
    L24: restore + re-read + --verify the writable M-mode trap/interrupt CSRs.
    mepc/mcause compared in both policies; mscratch/mtval/mie hybrid-only; mip
    re-read but excluded from verify (hardware-driven). state_diff policy split;
    rt_csr_survival.S extended to guard the round-trip.
    
    L26: the V-register transport scratch moved from a fixed in-RAM address to
    the TOP page of the shared mmap, ABOVE the program's --mem-size (scheme D).
    The driver maps one extra page (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes), caps --mem-size
    at 2G minus the page, and rejects an ELF whose static image reaches the
    reserved page (elf_load_top + cmd_run). Shared ABI gains
    HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES. No program layout can collide with the scratch.
    
    Demonstrators (tests/fixtures): break_vscratch / break_vscratch_top (L26),
    break_mcycle_write / break_verify_diverge (L25 time-variant-CSR caveat).
    Docs: limitations L24-L26 + L10, USER_GUIDE 2.5, CLAUDE.md V-State Transport;
    removed the stale gem5-switch-parity spec. Roadmap: vscratch_reservation.md.
    
    Bumps verilator submodule to 68b13cc.
